transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~63m | Attendees: Samir, Jenna (Redwood); Alex, Maya, Carlos (Horizon)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, appreciate it. quick round-robin?
[00:08] Alex (Horizon): Alex here, director of ai platforms. Maya from security, Carlos engineering. we're excited to see how Redwood can help with inference for our clinical summarization flows.
[00:20] Samir: great, goal for today is to scope a 90-day pilot, align on success criteria and the commercial guardrails - credits, what's included, path to procurement. Jenna will cover benchmark plan.
[00:35] Jenna (SE): hi all, quick note - we'll want representative prompts and a realistic traffic pattern, esp seq length distribution. we'll run latency and cost-per-token numbers and a quality check against your golden set.
[00:50] Alex: high level, our goal is to move from an internal GPU cluster (on prem) to either Redwood dedicated or hosted for eval. primary constraints: PII handling, latency under 450ms p50 for short summaries (~200 tokens) and cost target to be lower than our current infra by 15%.
[01:10] Maya: security checklist: SOC2 reports, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration for key management, and data residency concerns for EU patients. We will need those docs early to loop legal.
[01:30] Samir: understood. we can provide SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SSO and RBAC support, and discuss KMS for private deployments. For hosted pilots we offer tenant isolation and audit logs; dedicated or private gives you the stronger guarantees.
[01:50] Carlos: on volume, for the pilot we expect a steady 10 RPS with peaks up to 40 for short bursts. that's roughly 1.2M tokens/day at current throughput. does that align with what you normally test?
[02:10] Jenna: that's actually a good scale for benchmarking. we'll size GPU allocation and batching strategy accordingly. for the pilot credit allocation we typically map to token usage or a fixed credit amount - Samir will propose.
[02:30] Samir: commercial guardrails - our typical pilot package is a 90-day pilot with a credits bucket (example: $25k equivalent, or X tokens) that covers baseline usage and benchmark runs; overages billed at a discounted pilot rate. we can also offer a short dedicated pool if you need isolation during the run.
[02:50] Alex: can we see an example T&C? specifically we need clarity on data retention, logs, and what constitutes included vs billable usage.
[03:05] Samir: yes. we'll send a one-page pilot T&C plus the pricing worksheet. included items: baseline compute credits, 1 benchmark run (as agreed), support hours for SE assistance. Overage and dedicated infra options will be explicit.
[03:25] Maya: also need to know how KV cache and prefix caching is handled, whether logs contain PHI, and if there is an option to disable logging or rotate/hold logs for a set period.
[03:40] Jenna: technical note - we can run with request-level redaction, and we have options to disable persistent request logging. if you require KMS-backed encryption at rest we can arrange private deployment or dedicated enlistment with your KMS.
[03:58] Alex: timeline-wise, we want to start the pilot in mid-September. our procurement lead wants to understand path to contract if pilot is successful - PO vs SOW, expected timelines to production.
[04:14] Samir: typical path: trial/pilot -> pilot success review with metrics -> convert to reserved capacity (Dedicated) or enterprise contract. legal/ procurement usually takes 4-8 weeks depending on SAML/KMS clauses. we can provide a template SOW to accelerate.
[04:35] Carlos: for benchmarks, what do you need from our side?
[04:40] Jenna: representative prompt set, sample payload shapes (attachments, clinical notes length distribution), target throughput and SLO thresholds. we'll run a perf harness that reports latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens under different batch sizes and kv cache hit rates.
[04:58] Alex: for quality, we need a regression threshold - if hallucination rate increases by >3% compared to our golden set it's a fail. also measurements on factual accuracy for named entities.
[05:14] Samir: we'll capture those as success criteria: (1) latency p50 <450ms for 200-token summaries; (2) cost per token reduction >=15% vs baseline; (3) hallucination delta <=3% on your eval set; (4) security checklist satisfied.
[05:36] Maya: one concern - if we do hosted pilot, will logs be accessible by Redwood ops teams? what level of isolation?
[05:50] Samir: hosted has logical multi-tenancy with strict access controls; audit logs are available to you; Redwood engineers access is audited and limited. if that doesn't meet your policy we can do dedicated or private which gives you more control.
[06:08] Alex: ok. commercial - if the pilot goes well, we prefer a reserved capacity commit for predictable cost. For procurement, what's typical pricing model?
[06:20] Samir: reserved capacity is monthly/annual commits with lower unit pricing and guaranteed capacity. We can show three tiers in the worksheet: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved, and private on-prem pricing.
[06:32] Carlos: benchmarking specifics - can you run with our models or do we need to rehost?
[06:38] Jenna: we can run verified open models from our catalog that match your legal constraints; if you need a model you already own, Private deployment is the path. For the POC we'll recommend a model variant that balances latency and quality - we'll include quantization profiles and suggestions.
[06:58] Maya: security artifacts request: SOC2, ISO attestation, penetration test summary, data flow diagrams, and a short GDPR/data residency statement.
[07:12] Samir: noted - we'll package those with the pilot proposal.
[07:18] Alex: about credits - are they strictly dollar credits or token-based? we have bursty traffic so token buckets can be rough.
[07:28] Samir: we can offer either: a dollar-denominated credit that covers compute and tokens, or a token-equivalent credit. we usually define overage rates and a cap to avoid surprises.
[07:42] Jenna: for the benchmarking run, we'll simulate your expected traffic shape including spikes so the cost estimate is realistic. we'll also show how batching and cache hits change unit economics.
[07:58] Carlos: one technical ask: can we run an A/B between your hosted model and our on-prem model to compare latency/quality?
[08:06] Samir: yes, that's common. we can run parallel tests and show diff reports.
[08:12] Alex: procurement: we'd like a clear path from pilot -> PO to get us into production quickly. what's typical timeline if pilot metrics are hit?
[08:22] Samir: once pilot success is confirmed, we often have a commercial discussion and an SOW. If legal review is straightforward, 4-6 weeks to sign a PO for reserved capacity; if KMS/on-prem clauses are complex it can be longer. we'll work with your procurement to accelerate.
[08:41] Maya: will need to verify that audit logs and encryption meet our internal controls before sign.
[08:48] Samir: understood. we'll provide the artifacts and a security call.
[08:55] Alex: ok let's recap next steps.
[09:00] Samir: recap — Redwood will send pilot proposal with credits and T&Cs, Jenna will provision endpoints and plan the benchmark, Horizon to send sample payloads and security questionnaire. we'll aim to start pilot mid-September.
[09:15] Alex: sounds good.
[09:18] Maya: thanks everyone.
[09:20] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc.

Notes: transcript contains occasional auto-caption errors (e.g., KV cache -> K V cache). References to Redwood product names may be slightly off in places.
